newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangchak plans to raise 9.0 bln baht.
newsitem.headline: Bangchak plans to raise 9.0 bln baht.

text.p: The Bangchak Petroleum Plc planned to raise up to 9.0 billion baht (US$360 million) over three years to upgrade its refinery, a senior company official said on Friday.
The funds will be raised through loans and share flotation, Suwanna Langnamsung, head of BCP's public relations department told Reuters.

The company on Thursday named three financial advisers to help it offer 31 percent of its 522 million shares to the public and private sector. At present, the public holds about 20 percent of Bangchak's stake, and the rest is held by the finance ministry and two state-run agencies.
The advisers are Thai Investment and Securities Plc (TISCO), Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities Co, and Phatra Thanakit Plc.
Bangchak will also borrow US$90 million from the World Bank and 3.0 billion baht from both local and foreign financial institutions, Suwanna said.
"We will use the proceeds to improve the quality of oil from our refinery," she said.
BCP's current capacity is 120,000 barrels per day.
